editorial.headline: Premium Calls: Nationally Open, Clearly Read in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A premium-call operation is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not marked as blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Premium-call services under this code are defined by how the call is delivered. The activity is the operation of premium-tariff telephone calling services that use an intelligent-network (IN) premium-call access code to connect the caller with a premium-call agent and/or a recorded information service. Each part matters: it is a telephone calling service, the tariff is premium, and the connection uses the named intelligent-network access code. The agent and recorded-information routes are both within the stated scope: the and/or wording allows either connection as well as a combination of the two.

The scale field is equally direct. Micro, Small, Medium and Large are all listed as open to this activity, so the record does not confine premium-call service operations to one listed business size. The scale label sits beside a precise operational description: a registration at any of those stated sizes still concerns premium-tariff telephone calls, the IN access code, and a connection to a premium-call agent, recorded information, or both. It gives founders a clear account of who may register by scale without changing what the activity is.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The code is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. In ordinary terms, the national record permits a fully foreign-owned PMA registration for this activity. That is the full national ceiling stated for the code; it is not a partial foreign-share allowance. For a founder deciding whether this precise premium-call operation can sit in a foreign-owned company, the national answer in the record is yes, up to the stated 100% maximum.

Bali calls for a separate, equally plain reading. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This record, however, is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and its explanation says that, at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High—so it is not caught by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is not a workaround: this premium-call activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not moratorium-blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the supplied record. The Bali risk observation is expressly tied to the Large scale.
